entries.name: Aegis
entries.description: The Bulwark's big sibling - a shield that walks, built by someone who believed the best weapon is the enemy's wasted time.
entries.tactics: Fourteen HP of pure blockade with painful contact damage. Aegis walls come escorted - Wardens hide behind them lobbing homing bolts. Breaking the shield head-on costs seconds you may not have; going around costs position. Decide fast, commit fully.

entries.name: Bloodhound
entries.description: All muzzle, no leash. The host does not aim Bloodhounds; it releases them.
entries.tactics: A fast diver whose red dart turns viciously but gives up almost immediately. Sharp, short dodges beat wide ones - the dart cannot follow a quick cut. Two hits kill it; do it before the third pounce.

entries.name: Bulwark
entries.description: A slab of walking iron with no gun, no eyes, and no doubts. The host does not expect Bulwarks to win battles - only to make you late for them.
entries.tactics: High HP, slow descent, no attack; pure blockade. Behind one there is usually something shooting - a Warden's homing bolts curve around it. Either commit to breaking the wall fast or hold your fire and slip around; half-measures waste your damage into iron while the escort works.

entries.name: Chanter
entries.description: It rings a warning before its circle of bells tolls - not out of fairness, but ceremony. The host insists on its rituals.
entries.tactics: Telegraphs (pulses violet-white) before releasing an eight-bullet ring. The pulse is your timer: be moving AWAY when it fires, and the ring's gaps carry you through. Killing it mid-telegraph cancels the toll entirely.

entries.name: Colossus
entries.description: A fortress given legs and a grudge. Nothing gets through a Colossus until everything does - the host builds them to define where the battle happens.
entries.tactics: Massive HP (miniboss bar), heavy contact, slow walk, no gun. It is terrain that moves. Do not duel it while anything else shoots - use its own shadow as cover from enemies above it, and grind it down when the screen allows.

entries.name: Curseweaver
entries.description: It weaves your bad luck in advance and wears it as a robe. The violet eye is the loom. CURSED: killing it costs your sight.
entries.tactics: CURSED - killing it BLINDS you for four seconds (the screen closes in). It fires slow homing bolts, so ignoring it entirely is expensive too. The professional answer: kill it at a calm moment, blind on YOUR schedule. The aura pulse marks the price.

entries.name: Darter
entries.description: Fast, fragile, and utterly without fear. Darters are the host's messengers, and the message is always the same: you have less time than you think.
entries.tactics: Very fast, no gun - its body is the weapon. It crosses the screen in a couple of seconds, so treat every Darter lane as briefly poisoned. One hit kills it; snap shots work, but simply not being in its column is cheaper.

entries.name: Descender
entries.description: The rank and file of the endless host. Nobody remembers mustering them; they were simply always falling, rank after rank, like violet rain that learned to hold a spear. Alone, one is nothing. The host has never sent one alone.
entries.tactics: Falls straight down at a steady pace and fires a single green bolt straight ahead on a fixed cooldown. It never aims, so standing anywhere but directly beneath it is safe. Two hits end it - clear them early before bigger threats arrive, and never let a row of them fence you in.

entries.name: Direhound
entries.description: The host's kennel-master lost the argument about whether this one should be let out. Gold fangs, red eyes, miniboss bar.
entries.tactics: A 35-HP MINIBOSS howling telegraphed triple-bursts of homing bolts. The bursts track sequentially - keep a steady circle and they trail behind you like a comet tail. Its escort dies first; the hound is a patient grind that always drops a sword.

entries.name: DreadCaptain
entries.description: The host's field officer, all black iron and gold plume. Captains do not fall with their soldiers. They arrive where the fighting is worst, on purpose.
entries.tactics: A 30-HP MINIBOSS (tracked bar) firing telegraphed aimed triple-volleys in bursts of three. The volleys converge on your position - strafe THROUGH them, not away. Its slow march gives you time; its escort usually does not. Priority: escorts first, then the grind - it always drops a sword.

entries.name: Gemini
entries.description: Two orbs that share one grudge. They never fire together - the second waits for your dodge.
entries.tactics: Fires TWO red homing bolts in quick succession. The first pulls you, the second punishes the pull - keep moving through both instead of stopping after one. It weaves, so lead your shots.

entries.name: Grudge
entries.description: A scrap of the dark with one violet eye, drifting among the crowds you actually want to shoot. It wants to be killed. That is the trap.
entries.tactics: CURSED: killing it JAMS your gun for four seconds - it pulses a dark aura as warning. It has no weapon; its whole job is to swim between real targets and eat your stray bullets. Check your line of fire before you hold the trigger. Sometimes the strongest shot is the one you do not take.

entries.name: Harbinger
entries.description: A turning wheel of violet omens. What it announces has never once been good news.
entries.tactics: Fires a rotating six-bolt ring (violet, telegraphed) - each volley steps a few degrees, so the safe angle NEVER stays. Keep circling in one direction and the gaps come to you; freeze and the wheel finds you. Kill it during the telegraph pauses.

entries.name: Hexblade
entries.description: Twin blades that fell from the same forge and never separated. They snake as they fall, and the wall they draw between you and the sky bends like a living thing.
entries.tactics: Fires paired green walls that snake (sine motion - violet bullets). The wall's gap oscillates: watch one full period before committing to a lane. The Hexblade itself weaves fast; it dies in three hits if you can pin it.

entries.name: Hexer
entries.description: A quiet curse-monger. Hexers rarely kill anyone themselves; they make the sky complicated, and the complicated sky kills you.
entries.tactics: Fires slow crossing bolts on fixed diagonals. One Hexer is trivial; three turn the screen into a braid. Their shots are the slowest on screen - track them peripherally and prioritize the enemies forcing you to move.

entries.name: Hunter
entries.description: The host's bloodhound. It does not patrol, it does not guard - it points its whole falling body at where you are and corrects.
entries.tactics: Tracks your horizontal position while descending - it will be above you. Its dive is the threat; sidestep late and it cannot correct in time. Killing it early spares you the pressure entirely.

entries.name: Inquisitor
entries.description: A tall crimson hood with a white slit where questions come out. Its brands do not ask where you are. They ask where you will be.
entries.tactics: Telegraphs, then fires TWIN red homing brands in quick succession. The first pulls your dodge; the second punishes it. Break line by moving hard perpendicular through both, or kill it during the telegraph. High value target - never let two Inquisitors sync.

entries.name: Lamprey
entries.description: A pale worm that has never hurried and never let go. Its bolt remembers you longer than most friendships last.
entries.tactics: Its slow red bolt hunts for over TWO seconds - you cannot simply sidestep it once. Drag it in a wide circle until it dies of old age, and mind the wave around you while you babysit it. Kill the Lamprey first when possible.

entries.name: Lancer
entries.description: A splinter of steel with a single idea. The bolt it fires leaves the barrel almost lazily, as if stretching - then remembers its purpose all at once.
entries.tactics: Fires a green bolt that starts slow and accelerates hard. Your instinct calibrates on the launch speed and is wrong by the time it reaches you - dodge EARLY, when the bolt is born, not when it looks close. The Lancer itself dives fast; two hits kill it.

entries.name: Locust
entries.description: One is a whisper. The swarm is a sentence. Each carries a single tiny bite that knows your name.
entries.tactics: 1 HP, swarms, and every one spits a brief homing nip. Individually harmless - collectively they fill every lane you planned to use. Sweep them casually with spread fire and never let them accumulate behind you.

entries.name: Marauder
entries.description: Pressure incarnate. Marauders do not duel; they lean on you, volley after paired volley, until something - usually you - gives.
entries.tactics: Fires green arcs in quick two-bursts. The second burst comes fast after the first - never dodge into the space the first volley herded you toward. Mid HP; focus fire between bursts.

entries.name: Orbiter
entries.description: A violet ring that pins airspace the way a nail pins a map. The cross it fires is not aimed at you; it is aimed at everywhere you might want to go.
entries.tactics: Fires four bolts in a fixed diagonal cross, claiming lanes rather than chasing you. The gaps between the cross arms are always safe - learn the X shape and sit in its blind wedges while you burn it down.

entries.name: Penitent
entries.description: A grey figure that walks to be struck. Its penance is your weakness - literally. CURSED: killing it dulls your blade.
entries.tactics: CURSED - killing it applies WEAKNESS (-1 bullet damage) for four seconds. It never shoots; it just weaves fast through your line of fire like a confession you did not ask for. Fire discipline: shoot around it, or accept dull steel at a safe moment.

entries.name: Pyromancer
entries.description: Its fan of fire starts lazy, almost decorative - and then pounces like a cat that was only pretending to sleep.
entries.tactics: Fires an aimed three-bolt fan that ACCELERATES. The safe gap you see at launch closes fast - pick your dodge lane immediately and commit. Kill it high; an accelerating fan from low altitude is nearly unreactable.

entries.name: Ravager
entries.description: Slow, heavy, patient. A Ravager has never hurried in its existence, because its bolt does the hurrying - for a little while.
entries.tactics: Fires a red HOMING bolt that hunts you for about a second before flying straight. Red means hunted: move perpendicular and keep moving until it gives up the chase, then let it pass. High HP and heavy contact - respect its body too.

entries.name: Reliquary
entries.description: A dark shrine with a violet gem where a heart should be. Whatever is sealed inside was sealed for a reason - and your bullets are a key.
entries.tactics: CURSED miniboss: a 30-HP walking shrine whose death makes you LEADEN (slow) for four seconds. It blocks like an Aegis, so the temptation to break it is constant - but time your kill for a calm moment, or dodge around it and leave the seal alone. The aura pulse marks the price.

entries.name: Sentinel
entries.description: A patient eye in a bronze shell. Sentinels were the first of the host to look down and see YOU rather than a battlefield - and they have not looked away since.
entries.tactics: Descends slowly and fires single green bolts aimed at your position when it shoots. The bolt flies straight after launch: sidestep AFTER it fires, not before, or you dodge into the next one. Low HP - a priority target while it is still high on the screen.

entries.name: Seraph
entries.description: A white-violet wheel that sings when it turns. The host does not know where the Seraphs came from either. They arrived; the host made room.
entries.tactics: Weaves while releasing a rotating TEN-bolt wheel (telegraphed, violet). Dense but slow - hug the rim of one gap and rotate with it. The weave makes its position drift, so re-anchor after every volley. Twelve HP; commit real fire to it.

entries.name: Shepherd
entries.description: An amber ring that herds. The flock it drives ahead of itself is made of your bad options.
entries.tactics: Telegraphs, then releases a homing WALL of three - a fence that bends toward you. Do not outrun the fence; break its formation by cutting through the widest gap early, while the bolts still turn slowly. High HP; commit or avoid.

entries.name: Skirmisher
entries.description: A kite of red-brown leather that refuses to hold still. Skirmishers weave because a moving sniper is a living sniper - and they aim because living is not enough.
entries.tactics: Weaves while firing aimed green bolts. The weave makes it annoying to hit - lead its sine, or wait for the turnaround points where it briefly hangs. Its shots come at YOUR position: keep moving and they land behind you.

entries.name: Spinner
entries.description: It fell spinning once, by accident, and the host decided the terror was worth keeping. The spiral it trails has a hypnotist's patience.
entries.tactics: Sheds a slow rotating spiral of shots as it descends. Individual bullets are slow; the danger is the lattice they leave across lanes you wanted later. Cut it down early or accept fighting inside its web.

entries.name: Stalker
entries.description: A slit of red light on a falling shard of night. It has exactly one thought, and the thought is your coordinates.
entries.tactics: Fires a single red homing bolt that hunts you for about a second. Red means hunted: move perpendicular, let it commit, and step aside as it straightens. One at a time is practice; three at once is a lesson.

entries.name: Vulture
entries.description: Wings of night with a red appetite. It circles because everything beneath it is, eventually, carrion.
entries.tactics: Fires a homing PAIR in a narrow arc - two hunters with slightly different angles. Splitting them is the trick: drift one way until they commit, then cut back between them. It weaves; snapshot at the turnarounds.

entries.name: Warden
entries.description: A teal lantern that guards the walls. Wardens learned the oldest lesson of siegecraft: the archer behind the wall outlives the archer on it.
entries.tactics: The escort gun: slow, always behind a Bulwark or Aegis in the same lane, firing red homing bolts that curve around its shield. You cannot hit it until the wall dies - so either break the wall fast or dodge the bolts and starve it of a target. Red bullets hunt; keep moving perpendicular.

entries.name: Warlock
entries.description: It carries a ring of violet fire the way a monk carries a prayer - constantly, and for someone else's benefit. The detonation is the sermon.
entries.tactics: Descends and periodically releases a full ring of bullets in every direction. The ring is dense near the Warlock and sparse far away - distance is armor. Kill it between rings, and never fight it point-blank.

entries.name: Weaver
entries.description: A Descender that learned doubt. It swings across the sky as it falls, never quite committing to a lane, scattering short arcs of shot as if sowing a field.
entries.tactics: Weaves side to side while dropping and lobs a small green arc downward. Its position is predictable - a smooth sine - so lead it slightly when you shoot. The arc punishes you for standing still; keep drifting and it never touches you.

entries.name: Wisp
entries.description: A pale mote that would be beautiful if it were not so numerous. One Wisp is a firefly. Forty are a funeral.
entries.tactics: Tiny, fast, weaving, no gun - kills by touch. Swarms fill lanes faster than you can clear them; sweep them with your fire's natural spread while dealing with real shooters. Never chase one into a crowd.

entries.name: Zealot
entries.description: A blade of white gold that dives like judgement. Zealots believe - in what, nobody has survived long enough to ask.
entries.tactics: Very fast diver with an aimed bolt that accelerates viciously. Two threats in one: the bolt commits you to a dodge, and the diving body punishes the dodge. Kill it at the top of the screen or give its lane away entirely.

entries.name: Torchbearer
entries.description: Carries the fire that burns the maps of everywhere the host has been. Forward is the only direction left.
entries.tactics: Fast fodder with a short flame fan. Two hits and it is gone - the danger is the pace it sets, not the shots.

entries.name: Pikeman
entries.description: Rank and file of the host. The pike is longer than his patience and considerably longer than his life expectancy.
entries.tactics: A straight bolt on a steady march. Sidestep and cull - Pikemen only matter when something meaner hides behind their line.

entries.name: Falconer
entries.description: The bird is dead. He throws it anyway, and something in the dark keeps bringing it back.
entries.tactics: A weaving handler loosing red hunting bolts. Short sharp dodges beat wide arcs - the falcon gives up quickly. Kill him mid-weave when he drifts to an edge.

entries.name: Runescribe
entries.description: Every bolt is a word. The host's grammar is dreadful and entirely violet.
entries.tactics: Snaking violet script drifts down in sine waves. Read the wave, stand in the trough, and erase the author before the paragraph ends.

entries.name: Alchemist
entries.description: Turned lead into gold once. Now he turns distance into regret - his flasks arrive slower than they leave.
entries.tactics: Lobs aimed flasks that DECELERATE - fast at first, then hanging in the air where you wanted to dodge to. Treat old flasks as terrain, not bullets.

entries.name: Banneret
entries.description: The banner is heavier than the sword, which tells you everything about what the host thinks wins wars.
entries.tactics: A tougher aimed shooter that anchors formations. His shots are honest; his escort is not. Break the banner and the line around it loses its nerve (statistically).

entries.name: Ironmonger
entries.description: Sells iron. Delivers personally. Refunds are handled by the two tons of him walking at you.
entries.tactics: A 14-HP walking wall with painful contact and no gun. Like the Bulwark line: either commit to breaking it fast or route around and mind what shoots from behind it.

entries.name: Bellringer
entries.description: Rings the hour. The hour is always the same one: too late.
entries.tactics: Telegraphed rings toll outward on a slow clock. The gap in a ring is born where you were when it rang - keep moving BEFORE the toll, not after.

entries.name: Gravedigger
entries.description: Dug graves for the host until he noticed nobody was filling his. The shovel still works either way.
entries.tactics: CURSED - killing it drops Leaden on you (move speed crushed). The dark aura is the warning. Kill it only with room to be slow in, or route around it entirely.

entries.name: Martyr
entries.description: Died for the cause once already. The cause was not grateful. Now everyone gets to share the experience.
entries.tactics: CURSED - its death inflicts Weakness (-1 damage) for the duration. A weaving arc-shooter you often WANT to leave alive while heavier targets need full swords. Fire discipline.

entries.name: Dirgesinger
entries.description: The song has no words anymore. The bolts learned the melody and carry the verse themselves.
entries.tactics: Broad violet curtains, slow and wide. One Dirgesinger is a rhythm; two are a wall of music. Prioritize when the screen already snakes.

entries.name: Trebuchet
entries.description: Someone taught a siege engine to walk. Nobody taught it to stop.
entries.tactics: A slow engine hurling sweeping walls. The wall is level with its arm - flank it and the volley never reaches you. Ten HP of wood burns eventually.

entries.name: Blackguard
entries.description: Thrown out of the host's army for conduct unbecoming. The host has low standards, so imagine.
entries.tactics: A fast weaving duelist with aimed shots - closes distance while firing. Do not let it set the range; kill it at the top of the screen or dance with it.

entries.name: Riftling
entries.description: A splinter of somewhere else wearing a robe. The robe is doing most of the work of looking like a person.
entries.tactics: RIFT ELITE: opens a telegraphed rift AT YOUR POSITION and erupts spikes from it. The square marker is your one warning - move OFF the mark and the spikes miss. Expensive to field; kill it before its second cast.

entries.name: Voidcaller
entries.description: It is not calling the void. It is answering, and the connection is excellent.
entries.tactics: RIFT ELITE: rings erupt from random rifts in the upper field, raining outward. Watch for markers, claim the lower screen, and end the call at 8 HP before rings overlap.

entries.name: StandardBearer
entries.description: The standard has fallen eleven times. He picks it up every time. It is starting to look personal.
entries.tactics: An 18-HP MINIBOSS (tracked bar) firing telegraphed aimed volleys - a fair, killable duel that ALWAYS drops a wing. Strafe through the volleys and take the speed you will need.

entries.name: Ossuary
entries.description: A cabinet of everyone the host could not use whole. It rattles when it is aiming.
entries.tactics: A 22-HP MINIBOSS casting slow rings. The rings are readable and the march is glacial - it is a damage check, not a dodge check, and it ALWAYS drops a bolt for your trouble.

entries.name: Riftmaw
entries.description: A mouth that learned to open somewhere else. The teeth arrive before the rest of it decides to.
entries.tactics: A 20-HP RIFT MINIBOSS: rifts open on your position and spit short homing volleys. Hold the marker rule - off the square, sharp cuts against the red - and it ALWAYS drops a sword.

entries.name: Apocrypha
entries.description: The book the host reads before it falls. Nobody wrote it. It accumulates. Its last word is a hound.
entries.tactics: The rift endgame (difficulty 8, 1000 HP): crosses through curtains, then rift homing volleys over a spiral with Hexblade adds, and in the Last Word - dense rift rings, rift gyres, homing bolts, and a DIREHOUND MINIBOSS summoned into the fight. Bring full buffs, read every square, and never fight the hound inside a ring eruption.

entries.name: Archon
entries.description: A star of judgement that never learned mercy's spelling. Its wrath calls zealots; its ascension calls wardens; its light calls walls.
entries.tactics: Wide fans and rotating crosses, then sweeping walls plus Zealot summons (Wrath), then rings, homing bolts, and Warden summons (Ascension). The summons are the real pressure - clear Zealots before their dives sync with the walls. White tint means final phase: maximum speed, keep to the bottom corners.

entries.name: Behemoth
entries.description: A wall of iron that learned to fight back. Everything the Behemoth throws is heavy, including the silence between volleys.
entries.tactics: Accelerating fans, massive slow walls, offset and dense rings across three phases. Its bullets are heavy but sparse - the fight is about patience, not reflexes. Punish the long recovery after each wall; by Meltdown (red glow) the floor is mostly bullets, so pre-plan lanes.

entries.name: Eternity
entries.description: A white void ring that was here before the host and intends to be here after. Stillness. Motion. Eternity. It has only ever needed three words.
entries.tactics: Stillness lays cross-quads through sine curtains - deceptively calm; learn its spacing. Motion (65%) adds a spiral and Hexblade summons. Eternity (35%) is dense rings, storm crosses, and the gyre at 1.6x hover with Ravagers hunting you. The hardest fight in the game; every powerup cap and every color rule you have learned is the entry fee.

entries.name: The Executioner
entries.description: An axe-head the size of a doorway with a verdict already written. The squares it opens are not warnings. They are appointments.
entries.tactics: Random rift crosses plus muzzle homing bolts (difficulty 6). The crosses claim diagonals from wherever a square opens - the moment one appears, note its lanes and leave them. Verdict (55%) adds sweeping walls and Zealot summons: kill the Zealots between wall passes.

entries.name: The Gatekeeper
entries.description: The first bell of the Run. The Gatekeeper does not hate you; it simply was built into the doorway, and you are knocking. Every knight meets it. Most meet it again.
entries.tactics: The tutorial boss: aimed shots, a modest fan, a phase flip at half HP. Its openers are slow and generously spaced - use the fight to practice reading telegraphs and phase tints. If the Gatekeeper is costing you hearts, later gates will cost the run.

entries.name: Herald
entries.description: It announces the wall, then becomes it. The Herald believes a proclamation should be legible from anywhere on the battlefield - so it writes in bullets, edge to edge.
entries.tactics: Sweeping telegraphed walls with deliberate gaps, plus aimed jabs to herd you. Find the gap EARLY - the wall crosses slowly but totally. Below half HP (Judgement, white tint) a rotating cross joins; track the cross's turn and treat the walls as the metronome.

entries.name: Lich
entries.description: Green curtains of grave-light, swaying as they fall. The Lich conducts them like a choir, and below half health the phalanx begins to march.
entries.tactics: Sine curtains (violet snaking walls) with fast aimed spit underneath. The curtains breathe - their gaps slide in waves; move WITH the wave, not against it. Requiem (below half) adds a snaking phalanx wall: keep to the screen's lower third and thread the oscillation.

entries.name: Monarch
entries.description: The old king of the endless host. Three reigns, each crueller than the last, and a court of bullets that never stops bowing.
entries.tactics: Three phases stacking cross-quads, dense rings, and spirals. Phase entries are pulsed and tinted - the moment it flashes, reposition to open space before the new pattern's first volley. The dense ring's gaps are narrow but honest; the spiral rewards circling with it.

entries.name: Oblivion
entries.description: The last thing most far runs see. A near-black orb with a violet rim, dense rings, a turning spiral, and the dark that follows you home.
entries.tactics: Dense rings with aimed spit, then a spiral (Maw, plus Hexblade summons), then cross-quads with homing bolts and a Ravager (Oblivion phase). The rings are the rhythm section - everything else syncopates around them. Below 30% the hover doubles; stop aiming at where it is.

entries.name: The Riftwarden
entries.description: The first thing that learned doors do not need walls. Its frame IS the doorway, and the courtesy of a knock is a square of violet light.
entries.tactics: The rift tutorial boss (difficulty 5): telegraphed squares open AT YOUR POSITION and erupt rings a moment later - the square is where you WERE, so simply keep moving. Threshold (below half) adds random-position crosses: track two squares at once, never stand on either.

entries.name: Serpent
entries.description: Two fangs, one appetite. The Serpent crosses its own fire because it long ago stopped distinguishing between the battlefield and its jaws.
entries.tactics: Aimed spit from alternating fangs plus crossing diagonal volleys that lattice the screen. The lattice tightens as it bleeds - the fight gets harder as you win, so bank your dodging stamina. Stay off the centerline where the crosses overlap.

entries.name: Stormcaller
entries.description: The storm follows you. Crosses of violet lightning turn about the Stormcaller as it hunts, and the thunder always aims.
entries.tactics: Capped red homing bolts plus rotating StormCross volleys. The homing bolts give up after a second - bait them wide, then cut back. Tempest (below 55%) adds a radial ring and speed: the crosses keep rotating, so never park in a gap; ride it.

entries.name: Summoner
entries.description: It does not fight you. It invites others to - and rings its bell while you drown in guests. The glowing core is the invitation list.
entries.tactics: Fights entirely through adds: Wisps in Ritual, Skirmishers in Legion (below 55%), with aimed spit and a telegraphed ring for punctuation. Kill the summons FIRST or they multiply past control - but watch your fire discipline near its ring telegraph. Its own HP melts fast once the court is empty.

entries.name: The Tribunal
entries.description: Three pillars, one sentence. It reads the charges in rifts - first one square, then two, then everywhere.
entries.tactics: THREE rift patterns run simultaneously by the Second Reading (difficulty 7): gyres, rings, and crosses each claiming their own square. The screen becomes a calendar of eruptions - triage by timer, newest square first. It summons Curseweavers: now every kill decision has a price. The final phase adds dense rings; hold the bottom corners.

entries.name: Tyrant
entries.description: It wears its ring of fire like a crown, and its triple volleys are decrees. The Tyrant does not tolerate standing still. It barely tolerates moving.
entries.tactics: Aimed triple volleys plus a wide fan, with an offset ring in its late phase. The triples come at your position - constant strafing beats reaction dodging. When the ring appears, the safe wedges rotate; find one and migrate with it.

entries.name: The Voidmother
entries.description: A pale orb with five eyes, none of which blink. What it births is small, hungry, and shockingly numerous.
entries.tactics: The swarm boss (difficulty 7): rift squares erupt HOMING volleys - five hunters from a point of your recent past - while Locusts spill continuously. Clear Locusts with your natural spread; save deliberate aim for the mother. Womb of Nothing (30%) adds dense rift rings: the squares now demand immediate evacuation.

entries.name: Warbringer
entries.description: A crimson war-totem with a gold eye that has already counted your hearts. The Warbringer does not summon soldiers. It PROMOTES them.
entries.tactics: Muster opens with wide fans and lance walls while a DREAD CAPTAIN miniboss marches in - kill the Captain before Onslaught (60%) triples the Zealot pressure. Warpath (30%) is rings plus homing under maximum speed. This is the wall the 40k crowd hits: bring maxed powerups or bring patience.

entries.name: The Castellan
entries.description: The outer gate's warden-stone, animated by a garrison oath nobody was left alive to release it from. It did not abandon its post. It brought the post to you.
entries.tactics: The first warded Boss: a 30-point blue ward soaks every hit before its health moves - the blue bar is the ward, not the boss. Break it through the steady fans, watch the shatter, then the real fight begins at FULL health. Below half it is Unbarred: wide fans and offset rings, quicker on the hover. Patience through the blue, aggression after.

entries.name: The Baron
entries.description: A minor lord with a major opinion of himself, fighting the way he governed: from behind two people paid less than he is. The crown is real gold. The courage is outsourced.
entries.tactics: The first guarded Boss: his bar is GREY and he cannot be hurt while either Squire lives - do not waste a single arrow on him early. Drop both Squires (each pays out a powerup), watch him rage as the bar lights violet, then duel him honestly: aimed triples first, wide fans and rings below half. He hits harder than he deserves to.

entries.name: Baron's Squire
entries.description: Sworn to carry the Baron's shield and, apparently, to die holding it. Loyalty is not a virtue when the cause is a crown that shoots back.
entries.tactics: One of two guards that make the Baron untouchable - his greyed bar takes NOTHING until both fall. Squires are brittle (30 HP) but their bolts add up while you linger. Pick one, burst it down, then mirror it. Each fallen Squire pays a reward and drops a powerup for the real fight.

entries.name: The Plaguebearer
entries.description: It does not spread the plague. It carries it, gently, the way you carry something you love.
entries.tactics: A d2 curtain-caster that calls Wisps in while violet waves snake down. Kill the adds with strays, not swords - the curtains have troughs, live in them. Below half it Blooms: rings join the song.

entries.name: The Runesmith
entries.description: Forges the host's grammar one ring at a time. Complaints about the font are answered personally.
entries.tactics: Offset rings rotate around you - two interleaved circles whose gap drifts. Track the gap, not the bullets. Below half it Overwrites: a spiral joins and the gap starts moving twice.

entries.name: The Warlord
entries.description: Won every siege he ever laid by the simple expedient of never once going home.
entries.tactics: A 45-point iron ward - the blue bar - fronts a wall-thrower. Break the ward through sweeping walls and aimed shots, then the true Onslaught starts at FULL health: wide fans between the walls. Flank the walls; they sweep, they do not chase.

entries.name: The Gravewright
entries.description: The host's undertaker, promoted for enthusiasm. His work keeps getting back up, which he takes as a compliment.
entries.tactics: Summons CURSED help: Gravediggers early (their deaths slow you), Martyrs late (their deaths weaken you). Fire discipline is the fight - every add you reflex-kill hands him your legs or your sword. Red bolts hunt between waves of help.

entries.name: The Covenant
entries.description: An agreement between two places that should never have met. You are standing on the signature line.
entries.tactics: A pure rift-caster: crosses erupt on your position, then rings from random field-points once the Second Seal opens. The markers are the whole fight - stop watching the boss, watch the floor. Move off every square before it blooms.

entries.name: The Iconoclast
entries.description: Breaks holy things for a living. Wears the last cathedral it visited.
entries.tactics: An 80-point bone ward AND rifts - it casts the whole time you grind the blue bar, so the ward is not a free damage phase. Post-break the Desecration begins at full health: dense rift rings and rotating storm crosses. Budget your Purge for the second half.

entries.name: Regent's Blade
entries.description: The Regent owns two swords that walk. They have names. He has never used them.
entries.tactics: One of the Regent's two guards - 55 HP of aimed triples. While either lives the Regent's grey bar takes nothing. Split your attention: their volleys converge from both flanks. Each fallen Blade pays out and drops.

entries.name: The Regent
entries.description: Rules on behalf of a king nobody has seen in years. The arrangement suits him. The knight asking questions does not.
entries.tactics: Guarded by two Blades - he is untouchable and firing the whole time you duel them. Then three courts: fans and triples, dense rings below 55%, and a Scorched Court under a quarter where storm crosses sweep between walls. The endgame drill: kill the guard, bank a ward, spend it late.

entries.name: Pale Herald
entries.description: It announces the King the way frost announces winter: by already being everywhere.
entries.tactics: One of the Pale King's two heralds - and it casts RIFTS. While the pair lives the King takes nothing, and the floor keeps blooming crosses. Kill them fast or the marker density alone will end you. Each pays out and drops.

entries.name: The Pale King
entries.description: The throne was empty for a hundred years. Something patient sat down in it anyway. The host was never marching TOWARD anything - it was marching AWAY from him, and you are what is left in between.
entries.tactics: The d9 summit, every mechanic at once: two rift-casting Heralds guard him (grey bar), then a 150-point ward (blue bar), THEN three phases of ruin - dense rings into storm crosses into rift gyres with homing volleys while Riftlings pour in. Bank every Aegis and Purge you can carry. There is no trick. There is only being good enough. DU BIST GUT GENUUUUUG.
